blocking_defects.defect: The first 3.66 s (s1-shot-1 plan-overhead) are a static top-down floor plan. Its floor colour and light pool brighten over s1-event-1 (0.48 to 1.43 s) while the name plate settles under the plan (2.06 to 3.16 s). The plan's camera lamps stay at 0 until s1-event-3, which plays only after a hard cut into camera-ring-view at 3.66 s. B's own film_direction angle, opening_promise and divergence_note, and the registry note, all say B opens at the desk on the monthly counter and an empty turnover box. No s1 view draws a counter, a box or a ledger, so the declared treatment is not the executed one, and the executed opening is an establishing plan plus a title plate. Required result: the cameras visibly act within 1.5 s (as in A's correction), or implement the declared counter-first opening. Recognition of the plan at phone size stays unknown until pixels exist.

blocking_defects.criterion: dominant_action (the narrated transformation must be performed by its subject); source fidelity to c13
blocking_defects.defect: None of B's s2 views shows the system turning camera images into a timestamp. ledger-clock-desk draws the ring on a paper ledger with no system link (clockAt is called without fromCam). ledger-marker-row drops teal markers onto ruled paper rows titled 'Room clock record', with no camera and no pulse. The overhead turnover plan has no camera-to-clock link either; S.pulses is unused in every B view. A stamp landing on a ruled paper ledger invites the false inference of manual logging. That is the opposite of c13 ('automated, real-time documentation of perioperative events') and of the paper's point that events were captured independently of staff entry. Required result: in the n2a/n2b shots a wall camera visibly causes each stamp (A's camera-to-marker pulse is a working pattern), and the record surface does not read as a hand-kept ledger.

blocking_defects.defect: The opening is a brightening floor plan plus a name plate. The declared counter-first opening is not implemented.
The timestamps appear as stamps on a ruled paper ledger with no camera cause. That reads as manual logging, which contradicts automated documentation.
'Patient entry' is stamped on the table transfer; the roll-in happened earlier in s1.
At turnover the drape stays on the empty table as the patient leaves, and no reset is shown.
An identical undraped patient reappears on the table and is draped again, with no arrival.
The placebo row draws 12 units against the paper's 11, plus an unclaimed rank.
The camera company tag is clipped out of every n8b shot.
The camera lamps dim (shutdown inference), and the close omits the added cases it should answer.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain, from code (not observed): a floor plan of a generic Houston operating room brightens under a suite plate. A cut to wall height shows four cameras lighting, and on the plan a gurney enters under their sight wedges. A ruled 'Room clock record' ledger stamps entry, draping and turnover row by row, then an overhead plan stamps turnover as the patient leaves. A desk phone in a gloved hand lights and receives 'Patient draped' after a split-screen draping. The same study, percent, interval, placebo, associated-not-caused, bundle and stake boards follow on a ledger page. A future-work card tags turnover, and the film ends on a blank turnover box on the ledger in front of the room as its camera lamps dim.
story_review.opening_to_ending: It opens on the same question as A, but over a static plan, so the 'number first' promise is never shown. The answer arrives at s7. It closes on a blank turnover box on a desk ledger with the room's lamps dimming behind it. The ledger framing makes the record look hand-kept, which undercuts the 'camera logs the room' premise the ending relies on, and the close does not tie the open turnover question back to the 25 added cases.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2 to s3 (12.48 to 14.66 s). The overhead plan leaves the drape stranded on an empty table as the patient rides out on the gurney. The cut goes to a desk phone with no table, and then a split shows an identical undraped patient back on the table being draped again. Identity, the reset state and cause are all broken across the handoff.
